title: IDS's Nion 3D ToF camera goes into series production
summary: IDS has moved its Nion 3D time-of-flight camera into series production, offering high-resolution depth data at 30 fps with temporal stability under fast motion and shifting illumination. The significance is practical rather than speculative: it targets logistics, automation, and robotics systems that need reliable 3D perception at real process speeds.

extra.full_text: It provides high-resolution and temporally stable depth information at 30 fps, even during rapid movements and in changing lighting conditions. This makes it suitable for applications such as logistics, automation and robotics, where precise 3D data is required at real-world process speeds.

title: These tiny drones are powered by sound
summary: EPFL’s MICROBS Lab has built tiny microfliers powered by sound, using Helmholtz resonance: airflow over a small cavity generates pressure oscillations that can drive motion much like blowing across a bottle neck creates a tone. The approach points to a lightweight way to actuate very small drones without conventional onboard motors or bulky power systems, which is interesting for microrobots where every milligram matters.

title: Impossible Metals' Eureka II Recovers Itself From the Ocean, Fully Autonomously
summary: Impossible Metals’ Eureka II underwater vehicle demonstrated fully autonomous recovery off Halifax, locating its surface vessel underwater, aligning with it, attaching, and returning to the deck without manual control. The demo matters because autonomous docking and recovery are a major practical bottleneck for scaling ocean robotics, especially for long-duration subsea operations where human intervention is costly or impossible.

extra.full_text: New footage from Halifax shows the American ocean-technology company's underwater vehicle find its surface vessel beneath the waves, align, attach, and return to the deck with no human hand on the controls, clearing one of the gating hurdles to scalable ocean robotics.
